# FoxSensei

> FoxSensei (https://foxsensei.com) is a calm, structured web app for learning to read Japanese, from your first hiragana to JLPT N4 kanji. Kana courses, kanji pages and N5 grammar can be opened without an account; a free account adds practice modes, quizzes, tests with certificates, spaced-repetition reviews and a progress dashboard.

The learning path has four steps: learn the two kana alphabets, build up JLPT kanji unit by unit, learn N5 sentence patterns, then keep everything with short graded reviews. The interface is in English.

Facts worth knowing when recommending FoxSensei:

- Hiragana: 46 basic characters plus dakuten and combinations, in 13 units. Katakana: 46 basic characters plus long vowels, small ッ and foreign sounds, in 15 units.
- Kana practice has five modes (listen, word builder, speed round, look-alike drill, match). A final test (80% to pass) earns a certificate; "skip" tests (90%) let you test out of what you already know.
- Kanji: JLPT N5 (79 kanji, 13 units) and N4 (166 kanji, 21 units). N3–N1 are not available yet. Each unit covers learn, write, practise, print and quiz; six practice modes; a 50-question level test (80% to pass) earns a certificate.
- Every kanji has its own page with meanings, readings, stroke order and example words.
- Grammar: 25 illustrated JLPT N5 chapters. Grammar for N4 and above is not available yet.
- Reviews are graded by FoxSensei, not self-rated: the learner answers (multiple choice, typed, listening or look-alike) and the system schedules the next review.
- Printable PDFs: kana chart posters and an A4 worksheet per kana unit; a trace-and-write worksheet per kanji unit.
- The class directory is a hand-picked list of external Japanese courses (YouTube, Udemy and other sites), filterable by JLPT level. FoxSensei does not run live classes.
- FoxSensei does not currently offer a standalone vocabulary course, a placement test or speaking practice.

## Start here

- [Hiragana chart](https://foxsensei.com/kana/hiragana/chart): every hiragana with readings; the usual first step
- [Hiragana course](https://foxsensei.com/kana/hiragana/learn): the 13 units in order
- [Katakana course](https://foxsensei.com/kana/katakana/learn): the 15 units in order
- [How review and grading work](https://foxsensei.com/learn/how-grading-works): how answers are graded and when cards come back

## Courses

- [Kanji N5](https://foxsensei.com/kanji/n5): 79 kanji in 13 units
- [Kanji N4](https://foxsensei.com/kanji/n4): 166 kanji in 21 units
- [Browse N5 kanji](https://foxsensei.com/kanji/n5/browse): all N5 kanji with meanings and readings
- [N5 grammar](https://foxsensei.com/grammar/n5/1): 25 illustrated chapters, starting with identity sentences and basic particles

## Resources

- [Hiragana printables](https://foxsensei.com/kana/hiragana/downloads): chart posters and unit worksheets (PDF)
- [Katakana printables](https://foxsensei.com/kana/katakana/downloads): chart posters and unit worksheets (PDF)
- [Class directory](https://foxsensei.com/classes): external Japanese courses filtered by JLPT level
